metadata.title: Stock market today: Dow rises, S&P 500 and Nasdaq deepen losses as Anthropic IPO fails to quell AI worries

content.text:
US stocks mostly slouched again on Friday after Anthropic's (ANT) successful initial public offering wasn't enough to subdue broad uncertainty over artificial intelligence safety and financing.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) rose 0.4% after the blue-chip index fell below 50,000 and neared a correction. The S&P 500 (^GSPC) declined by 0.5% after six consecutive days of losses. The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) fell more than 1.5%.
Investor sentiment was subdued on Friday morning as Asian semiconductor stocks fell, suggesting further pressure on tech. Nvidia (NVDA) stock fell 3%, extending a six-day decline.
A day after its record-breaking debut, Anthropic shares fell 9% from a closing price of $97, though they remain above their IPO price of $83. After a big pop on its IPO day, Anthropic faces a test in the markets to see whether it can keep the momentum going.
49,583.70 +486.64 (+0.99%)
As of 10:00:35 AM EST. Market Open.
Other assets slid on Friday as well. Gold futures (GC=F) dropped 3%, while the price of digital gold — bitcoin (BTC-USD) — dropped below $62,000 to trade at its lowest price since July.
On the economic front, meanwhile, the University of Michigan's consumer sentiment will be the highlight, as gas prices have come down to below $4 per gallon.
LIVE 7 updates
The post earnings slide in Nvidia stock is getting uglier by the day
With Nvidia's (NVDA) stock falling another 3% Friday morning, the chip giant's post-earnings rout refuses to let up, Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi writes.
Shares of the fallen AI chip darling are down more than 10% since the company's Nov. 17 earnings report. The stock is down 14% since founder Jensen Huang resigned on Nov. 12 under a cloud of controversy, notably over his affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
Interim CEO and longtime CFO Colette Kress made a pretty compelling case this week that Nvidia can keep running the AI money machine without Huang in the driver's seat.
Read more:
Stocks open mixed as AI trade weighs on heels of Anthropic debut.
US stocks were mixed Friday as the blue chip Dow Jones Industrial Index rose, while selling pressure continued across tech stocks on the heels of Anthropic's IPO.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) climbed 0.5%, while the S&P 500 (^GSPC) declined by 0.5% and the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) fell 1.4%.
Anthropic (ANT) shares pulled back after surging in their public debut Thursday, while Nvidia (NVDA) extended its recent slide as weakness spread through semiconductor stocks. The S&P 500 entered Friday riding a six-session losing streak after all three major indexes dropped more than 2% Thursday.
Pressure was also visible beyond stocks, with gold futures sinking and bitcoin falling below $62,000. Investors will get another read on the consumer later Friday with the University of Michigan's final November sentiment survey.
49,583.70 +486.64 (+0.99%)
As of 10:00:35 AM EST. Market Open.
Nvidia stock extends 6-day losing streak, as AMD, Broadcom lead chip sector lower
Chip giant Nvidia (NVDA) extended declines on Friday, heading for seven straight days of losses. Peers AMD (AMD) and Broadcom (AVGO) also tanked 6% and 3%, respectively. US-based chipmaker Intel (INTC) stock also declined.
Memory chipmaker Micron Technology (MU) and peer SK Hynix (SKHY) also dropped more than 3%.
The broader chip sector fell on Thursday following the public debut of AI model maker Anthropic (ANT). The sector was already on shaky ground following the exit of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and concerns over AI financing.
142.09 -3.89 (-2.66%)
As of 10:00:35 AM EST. Market Open.
Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM) and equipment maker ASML (ASML) fell as well, leading the Technology (XLK) sector lower.
Other areas of the AI trade were under pressure, with optical equipment maker Coherent (COHR) and Bloom Energy (BE) stocks sinking 6% and 7%, respectively.
Read more.
Anthropic stock dives after rip-roaring IPO
Call it the Anthropic (ANT) IPO hangover.
Shares of the model builder dropped 13% in premarket trading on Friday as investors booked profits after a frenetic first day of trading. Not helping sentiment: The broader market plunged on Anthropic's well-received IPO day and remains under pressure today.
Anthropic made a monster debut on Wall Street Thursday, with shares opening at $111.50 a little before noon ET, a 34% premium to the $83 IPO price.
But the AI company's stock couldn't hold on to its early gains.
Read more.
92.30 -4.87 (-5.01%)
As of 10:00:35 AM EST. Market Open.
Anthropic's IPO ties the fate of the US economy closer to AI
Yahoo Finance's Hamza Shaban reports:
The day finally arrived. Anthropic (ANT) began trading on Thursday at $111.50 per share, surging above its $83 IPO price and briefly attaining a market capitalization of $2 trillion before settling into a still-respectable $1.2 trillion. What took years for the tech giants to achieve, the frontier AI lab grabbed in an instant.
But the historic IPO is notable not just for its size, but also for what it says — and will say — about the makeup of the stock market and the outsized influence of its largest players.
The top 10 biggest companies make up close to 40% of the S&P 500 (^GSPC). A bad day for tech means a bad day for the market. And now that Anthropic has joined the trillion-dollar ticker club — though it won't join the S&P 500 anytime soon — Wall Street's fate is tightly bound with another huge tech company, which also happens to be an AI lab without a long track record of financial stability.
Read more.
Dollar near 19-month peak as AI jitters sap risk appetite
Reuters reports:
The dollar held near a 19-month high on Friday, having risen over the past eight sessions as jitters over the AI trade sent investors fleeing to safe-haven assets, while the yen steadied after Japanese inflation data.
The dollar index was perched near the 103.9 level, its strongest since early April 2025, and was on track for a fourth straight week of gains. The rally accelerated on November 10, when hotter-than-expected US inflation data reinforced bets that the Federal Reserve would tighten policy. Markets are now pricing in a 25-basis-point hike in December and a small chance of a larger move.
Read more.

Mich. expectations, November final reading (50.9 prior); U. Mich. 1-year inflation, November final reading (+4.3% prior); U. Mich. 5-10 year inflation, November final reading (+3.4% prior); Kansas City Fed services activity, November (10 prior)
Earnings calendar: Bending Spoons (BSP), BJ's Wholesale Club (BJ), Moog (MOG-A), Frontline (FRO)
